picked.t: Vietnam motorbike tours offer different way to explore country
picked.body: Motorbike travel offers visitors a way to explore Vietnam beyond major tourist destinations, from winding northern mountain roads to forested central routes and riverside villages in the Mekong Delta. Unlike conventional sightseeing tours, motorcycle journeys allow travelers to explore at their own pace, stopping at local markets, rural communities and lesser-known attractions. Organized tours also provide local guides, route planning and logistical support. Northern Vietnam is popular with adventure riders for its mountainous terrain, limestone formations and winding roads. North Vietnam motorbike tours often include routes through Ha Giang, Cao Bang and Sa Pa, passing through valleys, terraced fields and villages inhabited by ethnic minority communities such as the Hmong, Dao and Tay. One of the region's best-known routes crosses Ma Pi Leng Pass, which overlooks the Nho Que River and surrounding limestone cliffs. Its steep slopes and sharp bends require experience, particularly in rainy or low-visibility conditions. In central Vietnam, sections of the historic Ho Chi Minh Trail offer a mix of natural scenery and wartime heritage. Riders can travel along the Truong Son mountain range, visit historical sites around Khe Sanh and explore the caves and countryside of Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park. Further south, the Mekong Delta offers a slower-paced experience, with relatively flat roads connecting orchards, coconut groves, canals and rural communities. Travelers can visit riverside towns, cross waterways by local ferry and explore traditional markets, although narrow roads and traffic still require caution. Beyond the scenery, Vietnam motorcycle tours provide opportunities to experience local life. Guided itineraries often include village visits, market stops and overnight stays at family-run accommodations. In northern mountain areas, some tours offer homestays in traditional stilt houses, where visitors can sample regional dishes such as freshwater fish, smoked meats, mountain vegetables and bamboo shoots. These shared meals and interactions with host families can offer insight into local customs and food traditions. Riders should avoid alcohol before and during their journeys. Motorcycle travel requires preparation, especially on mountain routes where weather, road surfaces and visibility can change quickly. Choosing a suitable bike is important. Lightweight dual-sport models such as the Honda CRF300L and CRF250L are designed for mixed terrain, while adventure motorcycles such as the CFMOTO 450MT may suit some routes. Riders should consider the motorcycle's weight, handling, seat height and luggage capacity, as well as their own experience. Protective equipment should include a certified helmet, riding jacket, gloves, abrasion-resistant trousers and sturdy boots. Foreign visitors should check Vietnam's licensing requirements before riding. Depending on their nationality and license category, an International Driving Permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention may be recognized when accompanied by the relevant national driving license. Travelers should confirm that their documents cover the motorcycle category they intend to ride and that their insurance includes motorcycle use in Vietnam. For remote mountain routes, an experienced local guide can help with navigation, accommodation and mechanical problems. Some guided tours also provide support vehicles, spare parts and assistance in areas with limited mobile coverage. Hanoi-based operator Vietnam Motorbike Tour Expert offers organized motorcycle journeys across the country. From northern mountain passes and central Vietnam's historic trails to the Mekong Delta's rural roads, motorbike tours offer an alternative way to explore the country's regional landscapes and communities. Proper equipment, valid documentation and careful route planning are essential for a safer journey.

picked.t: New Ho Chi Minh City chairman pledges to tackle traffic congestion, flooding
picked.body: In his six-minute speech after being elected chairman of the HCMC People's Committee on Thursday morning, Phong identified addressing four major issues assigned by General Secretary and State President To Lam as key priorities: traffic congestion, flooding, environmental pollution, and building a drug-free city. The new chairman stated he would focus on implementing the city's master plan through 2050, with a 100-year vision. This includes developing a green, clean, and attractive urban environment, alongside improving cultural, educational, and healthcare services to elevate the overall quality of life for residents. "These are the tasks on which the HCMC People's Committee chairman will devote his time and efforts to finding effective solutions, ensuring swift implementation, and achieving positive results," he said. Phong replaces Nguyen Van Duoc after receiving unanimous support from all 112 delegates present at the meeting. The 48-year-old previously served as first secretary of the Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union and secretary of the Dong Thap Provincial Party Committee. Before his election as city chairman, he was the standing deputy secretary of the HCMC's Party Committee. Phong highlighted several advantages driving the city's development. These include preferential mechanisms and policies, a competitive workforce, and the dynamic, innovative traditions of the localities recently merged to form the expanded municipality, specifically the former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces. The results achieved in the first year of the current term provide a foundation for the municipal administration to continue its work. The goal is to turn HCMC into a leading growth engine for the region and a major contributor to the national economy, despite ongoing difficulties and challenges. Beyond addressing urban problems, Phong identified other key tasks, such as translating development strategies into concrete plans. He emphasized building a growth model based on science and technology, innovation, and digital transformation, while pledging to maintain double-digit economic growth throughout his term. He committed to working with the municipal administration to maintain unity, discipline, and order. He also promised to listen to feedback and proposals from residents, businesses, scientists, and intellectuals to mobilize resources for development. At the meeting, HCMC Party Committee Secretary Tran Luu Quang stated the city faced a massive workload as its development space and administrative scale expanded alongside the introduction of new policy mechanisms. The primary priority following the leadership transition is to ensure continuity and keep the administrative apparatus operating smoothly. "The leadership transition must not slow down work," Quang stressed. Ongoing projects must be accelerated, issues that have already received policy approval must be addressed, and matters awaiting resolution by residents and businesses must not face further delays. Quang noted that Phong brings experience from both central and local levels, having demonstrated responsiveness and determination as standing deputy secretary of the municipal Party Committee. He expressed confidence that the new chairman would improve the effectiveness of policy implementation. In the immediate term, the city must implement its master plan and the Law on Urban Development using new policy mechanisms. Other immediate tasks include accelerating major infrastructure projects, addressing traffic problems, upgrading urban areas, and improving the environment. Additional priorities include developing science and technology, promoting innovation, establishing an international financial center, and creating new growth drivers. The city Party chief urged Phong to quickly take charge and work with the municipal administration to identify priority tasks. He advised coordinating with government agencies to tackle difficult and long-standing issues. Administrative performance must translate into tangible improvements visible to residents and businesses, Quang added. Following the regional merger, HCMC now has a population of more than 14 million and an economy worth over US$120 billion, accounting for approximately 23% of Vietnam's GDP. The city aims to rank among the world's 100 leading cities by 2030, establishing itself as a modern urban center and a regional hub for innovation. The new chairman takes office as the city intensifies efforts to meet its economic targets for the year. Gross regional domestic product (GRDP) grew by 9.06% in the first nine months. To achieve the full-year target of 10.2%, growth must exceed 13% in the final quarter. State budget revenue reached nearly VND762 trillion (US$29 billion) in the first 10 months. To meet its VND1 quadrillion target, the city must collect more than VND238 trillion over the final two months, averaging over VND3.9 trillion per day. Public investment disbursement has already exceeded 80%.

picked.t: 한국서 숨진 베트남 근로자, 배상금 한국 소득 적용할까? [양원준 변호사의 리걸 비나]
picked.body: 법무법인 법승 서울사무소 양원준 형사전문변호사 국내 체류 외국인이 260만 명을 넘어선 가운데, 베트남 국적자는 중국에 이어 두 번째로 많은 약 25만 명에 이른다. 이들 다수는 비전문취업(E-9) 비자로 입국해 제조업과 건설업 등 산업 현장의 핵심 인력으로 일하고 있다. 그러나 안타깝게도 이들이 작업 중 사고로 사망하거나 중상을 입었을 때 손해배상금이 어떻게 책정되는지 정확히 아는 이는 드물다. 흔히 "한국 사업장에서 일하다 다쳤으니 전액 한국 소득 기준으로 배상받겠지"라고 짐작하지만, 실제 법원의 판단 구조는 그리 단순하지 않다. 가장 먼저 짚어야 할 대원칙은 준거법이다. 국내에서 발생한 불법행위로 인한 손해배상 청구에는 피해자의 국적이나 유족의 본국 거주 여부와 무관하게 원칙적으로 대한민국 법이 적용된다. 따라서 손해배상액의 핵심인 일실수입 산정과 위자료, 과실상계 등은 모두 한국 민법과 대법원 판례의 법리에 따라 엄격히 판단된다. 여기서 가장 치열한 쟁점이 되는 항목은 사고가 없었더라면 미래에 벌었을 돈인 ‘일실수입’이다. 대법원은 일시 체류 후 출국이 예정된 외국인의 일실이익 산정에 관해 확고한 ‘이중 기준’ 법리를 확립해 두었다(대법원 1998. 9. 18. 선고 98다25825 판결). 국내 체류가 합리적으로 예상되는 기간 동안은 한국에서의 수입을 기초로 계산하고, 그 기간이 끝난 뒤 가동연한(일할 수 있는 나이의 상한)까지는 출국 후 본국에서 얻을 수 있는 수입을 기초로 나누어 계산한다는 원칙이다. 이는 네팔, 방글라데시, 우즈베키스탄 등 국적을 가리지 않고 하급심에서 일관되게 적용되고 있다. 그렇다면 국내 체류가능기간은 어떻게 결정될까. 법원은 단순히 체류허가서상의 만료일만 보지 않고 입국 목적, 사고 당시 본인의 의사, 비자 종류, 체류기간 연장의 실적이나 개연성 등을 종합적으로 살핀다. 통상 E-9 비자의 경우 기본 3년에 재고용 허가를 통한 연장까지 고려해 최대 약 4년 10개월 안팎을 한국 소득 인정 구간으로 보며, 그 이후부터 가동연한까지는 베트남 소득을 적용하는 것이 일반적이다. 이 원칙은 불법체류자에게도 원칙적으로 동일하게 적용되어 배상 청구 자체를 막지는 않지만, 체류가능기간이 지극히 짧게 인정되거나 아예 배제될 수 있어 실질적인 배상액이 크게 줄어드는 결과를 낳는다. 반대로 이미 재외동포(F-4) 비자처럼 장기 체류 자격을 얻어 정주성이 인정된다면 가동연한 전체를 한국 소득 기준으로 산정받기도 한다. 적용되는 소득의 기준 역시 면밀히 따져야 한다. 국내 체류기간에는 실제 소득을 원칙으로 하되, 실제 소득이 도시일용노임보다 낮더라도 일반노동에 종사할 개연성이 구체적으로 인정되는 경우에는 실제소득보다 높은 도시일용노임을 적용받을 수 있다. 반면 체류기간 종료 후 적용되는 베트남 소득은 원칙적으로 귀국예정인 베트남에서 얻을 수 있는 소득을 기준으로 산정한다. 보통 변론 종결일을 기준으로 베트남 근로자의 월 평균 임금을 기준으로 산정하나, 베트남 근로자의 성별, 직종별 평균 임금, 베트남 통계청 또는 공신력 있는 기관의 임금자료를 바탕으로 결정되기도 한다. 일할 수 있는 나이를 몇 세로 볼 것인가 하는 가동연한 문제도 중요한 변수다. 사고가 없었더라도 본국으로 돌아갈 예정이었다면 국내 기준인 만 65세가 아니라 본국의 법정 정년이나 사회·경제적 여건, 평균여명 등을 종합한 본국 기준 가동연한이 적용될 수 있다. 이는 배상 책임이 있는 피고 측에서 배상 총액을 낮추기 위해 적극적으로 다투는 지점이기도 하다. 한편, 외국인 근로자 역시 국내 산업재해보상보험법의 전면적인 보호를 받는다. 산재보험급여를 수령했더라도 사업주 등을 상대로 한 민사 손해배상 청구는 별도로 가능하다. 이때 동일한 성질의 손해에 대한 중복 지급을 막기 위해 보험급여를 공제하는데, 대법원은 ‘공제 후 과실상계’ 원칙을 취하고 있다(대법원 2022. 4. 14. 선고 2021다252472 판결). 총 손해액에서 먼저 산재보험급여를 뺀 뒤 남은 금액에 피해자 과실 비율을 적용하는 방식으로, 과실상계를 먼저 하고 공제하는 방식보다 피해자에게 훨씬 유리하다. 구체적으로는 휴업급여를 휴업기간 중의 일실수입에서 공제하고, 장해급여는 그 이후의 일실수입에서 각각 대응시켜 공제한다. 결국 외국인 근로자의 인명 사고를 둘러싼 손해배상 실무는 정밀한 법적 계산의 영역이다. 사고 당시 체류자격과 기간 만료일 파악은 물론, 비자 연장 가능성의 입증, 베트남 현지 소득 통계의 조기 확보, 산재급여의 올바른 공제 산식 적용 여부에 따라 최종 배상액은 수천만 원에서 수억 원까지 차이가 난다. 외국인 근로자의 수가 날로 늘어나는 오늘날, '국내 소득과 본국 소득의 이중 구조'라는 법원의 확립된 잣대를 정확히 꿰뚫어 보는 것은 피해자의 권익 보호와 합리적인 분쟁 해결 모두를 위한 필수 과제다. ※법무법인 법승 서울사무소 양원준 형사전문변호사

picked.t: Vietnam's largest island Phu Quoc reports $2.4B tourism revenues in 10 months
picked.body: The Vietnam's largest island received 9.2 million tourist arrivals in the first 10 months, up 30% year-on-year, including 2.14 million foreign tourists, a 59% increase year-on-year and surpassing its full-year goal of 2 million. In October alone, the island generated VND5.1 trillion in tourism revenues, up 37.8% year-on-year as foreign tourist arrivals surged 50% to 223,000, according to An Giang Province's Department of Tourism. The strong growth reflects Phu Quoc's growing appeal as a holiday destination, underpinned by investment in tourism infrastructure and a wider range of visitor experiences. Improved air connectivity has also helped attract international visitors, with direct flights linking the island to key markets such as South Korea, Central Asia and Eastern Europe. Phu Quoc's peak tourist season runs from November to April, coinciding with the island's dry season, which typically brings sunny weather, calm seas and low humidity.

picked.t: Busy expressway to Vietnam's largest airport Long Thanh widened to 12 lanes
picked.body: The interchanges with National Highway 51 and the Bien Hoa-Vung Tau Expressway on the HCMC-Long Thanh Expressway are taking shape. The two are key traffic hubs linking Long Thanh airport to the road network of Vietnam's southeastern region. The project to widen the HCMC-Long Thanh Expressway is about 81% complete after more than a year of work and is entering its final push to be largely finished this year. The roughly 22-km project, which broke ground in August 2025 with a total investment of more than VND16.3 trillion (US$634 million), runs from the Ring Road 2 interchange in HCMC to the Bien Hoa-Vung Tau Expressway in Dong Nai. Once complete, it will improve connections between central HCMC and Long Thanh airport, which is expected to begin operating at the end of this year.

picked.t: Floods sever roads, swallow excavators, inundate hundreds of homes in central Vietnam
picked.body: Floodwaters rushing downstream into the Cai River on Nov. 10 submerged several excavators at the Thac Ngua Bridge construction site linking Khanh Hoa Province 's Khanh Vinh and Trung Khanh Vinh communes. Strong currents overturned one piece of heavy machinery, leaving only its wheels exposed. The waters nearly swallowed the remaining excavators, leaving just their booms visible above the surface. Local authorities have yet to fully assess the property damage, though early reports indicate no casualties. Photo by Ha Le My Heavy rainfall in Da Nang City inundated the central area of Tra My Commune, prompting residents to evacuate to safety. Severe downpours between Nov. 9 and 11 battered central Vietnam, with the most intense precipitation occurring in Hue, Da Nang, and Quang Ngai. Multiple areas recorded rainfall exceeding 500 mm. Tra Thanh in Quang Ngai saw over 630 mm, while Tra Giap in Da Nang received nearly 553 mm. Rains are expected to ease from today. In Dak Lak Province , floodwaters surging down the Ky Lo River—which forms the boundary between Tuy An Bac and Tuy An Nam communes—swept away heavy equipment and steel materials at the Tam Giang weir construction site, where repair and rebuilding efforts were actively underway. The rapidly rising waters also triggered severe riverbank erosion, posing a direct threat to several riverside homes as well as the construction site itself.
